issues.failure_explanation: In OptEMA-M, alpha_t = rho_t^{-1/2} is a function of g_t = grad f(x_t;xi_t). Hence z_t = (1-alpha_t)(s_{t-1} + grad f(x_{t-1}) - grad f(x_t)) is not measurable with respect to the past, and E<z_t, alpha_t(g_t - grad f(x_t))> = E[alpha_t(1-alpha_t)<s_{t-1}+..., g_t-grad f(x_t)>] is not zero in general (alpha_t(1-alpha_t) is correlated with g_t). The Pythagorean identity used to obtain the recursion is therefore invalid; likewise the step alpha_t^2 E||g_t-grad f||^2 <= alpha_t^2 E||g_t||^2 treats the random alpha_t as a constant. Moreover the proof of Lemma sum:tail (and eq:alpha:s in Lemma M:sum:s) then uses this expectation-only inequality pathwise: it multiplies it by the random weights 1/(2 mu(1+tau_t)) and gamma_t(1+tau_t)^2 and substitutes ||s_t||^2 <= ||s_{t-1}||^2 + B_t as if it held almost surely.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either decouple alpha_t from the current sample (e.g. use rho_{t-1} in the EMA weight, changing the algorithm) or supply a genuine decoupling/martingale argument controlling the cross term, and must redo Lemma sum:tail with pathwise (not expectation) inequalities before multiplying by data-dependent weights.
issues.overall_effect: The whole OptEMA-M chain (weighted tracking-error bound, logarithmic bounds on objective/gradients, cumulative bounds, and Theorem the:it:EMA:M) rests on an unproved recursion; the convergence rate for OptEMA-M is unsupported whenever sigma>0.
issues.title: Tracking-error recursion drops a nonzero cross term because the EMA weight alpha_t depends on the current sample
issues.why_classification: The defective recursion is the core of the OptEMA-M analysis; a naive pathwise Young-type fix changes the noise term from alpha_t^2 to alpha_t and destroys the claimed rate, so new proof architecture (or an algorithm change) is required.

issues.failure_explanation: From gamma_t <= 2 alpha_t/(mu(1+tau_t)^2) one obtains alpha_t >= gamma_t mu (1+tau_t)^2 / 2, so (1-alpha_t)||s_{t-1}||^2 <= ||s_{t-1}||^2 - (1/2) gamma_t mu (1+tau_t)^2 ||s_{t-1}||^2, not with coefficient 2 as written. The claimed inequality uses the bound in the wrong direction; the subsequent constants (the '(1+4)B_t' step and C_w) inherit this.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the factor 2 by 1/2 in step 1 and propagate the constant (multiply the final coefficient of B_t and of ||s_0||^2 by 4), redefining C_w accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: Only the numerical constant C_w is affected (it should be about four times larger); the logarithmic form of the bound is unchanged.
issues.title: Wrong direction of constant in the sum:tail descent step (factor 4 off)
issues.why_classification: A local constant correction preserves the statement up to an absolute constant.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: There exists constants $C_f,C_g\geq 0$ such that $\EEE[f(\x_{t})] - f^* \leq C_f \ln(e + t)$, and $\EEE[\|\nabla f(\x_t;\xi_t)\|^2]\leq C_g \ln(e+t)$.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma G:bound gives only E||g_t||^2 <= C_g ln(e+t) and E[f(x_t)-f*] <= C_f ln(e+t). The proofs of Lemmas M:sum:s and M:sum:m use these as almost-sure bounds: tau_T = max_t ||g_t|| <= sqrt(C_g ln(e+T)), ||g_t||^2 <= C_f ln(e+T), f(x_t)-f* <= C_f ln(e+t) inside products with other random quantities (tau_T times ln(e+sum||g||^2), (1+tau_T)/gamma_T times max_t hat f_t, (1-alpha_T) max_t ||s_t||^2), and also E[max(||m_{t-1}||^2,||g_t||^2)] <= max_i E||g_i||^2, which is false (E max >= max E). Under bounded variance alone, E[tau_T^2] can be of order T sigma^2 (e.g. noise equal to ±sqrt(T)sigma with probability 1/(2T)), so no logarithmic bound on tau_T follows from the assumptions when sigma>0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must establish high-probability or expectation bounds on the joint products (e.g. E[tau_T^2 rho_T^{1/2}], E[max_t hat f_t / gamma_T]) without assuming pathwise logarithmic control of tau_T and f(x_t), or add a bounded-gradient/bounded-noise assumption, which would withdraw the advertised assumption-free scope.
issues.overall_effect: The bounds E sum||s_t||^2 <= C_s rho_T^{1/2} ln^{3/2} and E sum||grad f||^2 <= C_o(...) are unsupported for sigma>0; with only the available E[tau_T^2] <= T C_g ln(e+T), the 1/gamma_T <= mu(1+tau_T^2)rho_T^{1/2} term becomes of order T, destroying the T^{-1/4} stochastic rate of Theorem the:it:EMA:M. The deterministic case sigma=0 is unaffected since expectation and pathwise coincide.
issues.title: Expectation bounds on ||g_t||^2, f(x_t)-f* and tau_T are used pathwise (and E[max] bounded by max E) in the OptEMA-M cumulative bounds
issues.why_classification: The stochastic regime of the main OptEMA-M rate loses its support and a standard fix requires additional assumptions (contradicting the paper's central claim) or a substantially new argument.

issues.failure_explanation: The bound Theta_t <= sum_j prod(1-alpha_k)(E_j - D_j) is derived only in (conditional) expectation, because step 3 of the Gamma_2 bound replaces g_t by grad f(x_t) using unbiasedness. In the final descent step this inequality is multiplied by theta gamma_t, where gamma_t = (1+mu tau_t)^{-1}(1+sum_{j<=t}||m_j||^2)^{-1/2} depends on g_t (through tau_t and m_t). E[gamma_t <grad f(x_t), g_t/(eps+sqrt(v_{t-1}))>] is not equal to E[gamma_t <grad f(x_t), grad f(x_t)/(eps+sqrt(v_{t-1}))>] since gamma_t and g_t are correlated, so eq:OptEMA:V:suff:dec is not established. Lemma lamma:bound:sum:nabla compounds this by dividing the expectation inequality by the random gamma_t.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must decouple the stepsize from the current sample (e.g. use gamma_{t-1} or statistics up to t-1 in the update, changing the algorithm) or supply a decoupling argument controlling E[(gamma_t - gamma_{t-1})<grad f, g_t - grad f>]-type terms.
issues.overall_effect: The one-step descent inequality for OptEMA-V and everything built on it (logarithmic objective/gradient bounds, cumulative gradient bound, Theorem the:it:EMA:V) is unsupported whenever sigma>0.
issues.title: OptEMA-V descent inequality multiplies a conditional-expectation bound by the sample-dependent stepsize gamma_t
issues.why_classification: The defect sits in the foundational inequality of the OptEMA-V analysis; fixing it requires either changing the algorithm or a new nontrivial argument of the kind absent from the paper.

issues.failure_explanation: The preceding line carries the factor 1/(mu^2 eps^6); the next line replaces it by 1/eps^6 with no justification. Since mu in (0,1), 1/mu^2 > 1 and cannot be dropped. Carrying the factor gives (1+tau_t)/mu^2 <= (1+mu tau_t)/mu^3, so c_2 should be 2 theta/(mu^3 eps^6), not 2 theta/(mu eps^6).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine c_2 := 2 theta/(mu^3 eps^6) in the lemma statement and downstream constants.
issues.overall_effect: Only the constant c_2 (and hence C_o in Lemma lamma:bound:sum:nabla) is affected; the functional form of the bounds is unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma G:bound:2 controls only E||g_t||^2 and E[f(x_t)-f*]. The proof nevertheless asserts 1+tau_T <= iota sqrt(ln(e+T)) pathwise (eq:iota:2) and bounds E[(max_t hat f_t)(1+mu tau_T) sqrt(1+M)] by C_f ln(e+T) (1+mu tau_T) sqrt(1+M), i.e. it treats max_t f(x_t)-f* and tau_T as deterministic logarithmic quantities inside products of random variables. Under bounded variance alone E[tau_T^2] may be of order T sigma^2, so the claimed ln^{1/2} and ln^{3/2} factors in Term I, Term II and Term III are unsupported for sigma>0.
